findings.requirements: The RR4 regression gate cannot fail on the three sites it exists to protect. twmerge-class-resolution-all18.mjs:89 computes isKnown with clauses that are unconditional on the whitelist entry — c.id.includes('priority row') || c.id.includes('predictive row') || c.id.includes('photoCountButton') — so E6/E7/E12 can never increment unexpectedMoves. Reverting the RR1 fix leaves the gate at exit 0 with a summary line identical to the passing run. This is the project's own named Sprint 52 defect class: a blocking gate that silently never fires. The whitelist must key on the expected delta SIGNATURE for each site, so that a different delta — or a delta where none is expected — still reddens.

OVERLAY DECLARATION ADDED (twMerge had deleted the utility before)' on rows whose before and after strings are byte-identical ('text-destructive font-bold'). The detector only tests whether an overlay utility reached the element BEFORE; it never checks whether the after side carries a module class — an assumption inherited from the reviewer's own round-1 9-case witness, which stopped holding the moment RR1 began omitting the module class conditionally. The report then rationalises the false positive: 'RR1/RR2 fixed them at the CSS-module level, not by restoring the deleted-utility className behavior.' For E6b/E7b that is wrong — `!priorityOver && styles.metricRow` is precisely restoring it. The summary should read moved: 1 (E12 only), and the submission's 'class-list identity … zero delta' claim should match its own artifact.

findings.requirements: P0 because it defeats RR3/AC3 directly: the rework contract required a comparator that measures real before/after values or fails closed, and for this witness it does neither. Both PerfDevOverlay Part B cells report rgb(0, 0, 0): .text-destructive{color:var(--destructive)} -> globals.css:411 --destructive: var(--brand-900) -> :365 --brand-900: var(--mantine-color-brand-9), which MantineProvider injects at runtime and which is absent from .next/static/css. In a bare harness page the chain is unresolved, the declaration is invalid at computed-value time, and color falls back to the UA default for a <button>. The comparator scores that fallback as agreement instead of rejecting it, so the cell can neither confirm the fix nor detect a break on the property under test. §R2 attributes the difference to 'a purpose-built reduced stylesheet vs the full concatenated bundle' — the symptom, not the cause — and cites oklch(0.58 0.22 27) as the reviewer's measurement of 'the real production value'; that was a placeholder in the reviewer's own harness, now labelled as such, and the real value is #8E322B. The cell would still have caught an unfixed state, because the module rule resolves without Mantine's runtime variables, which is why this is a P0 in the apparatus and not a rendered regression. Fix: inject Mantine's runtime custom properties into the harness page, or assert that a measured value is not the property's initial/UA default and fail the cell when it is.
